sentences.text: The nearly complete skeleton of an adult Longicrusavis preserves carbonized feathers showing visible coloration on the head and forelimbs. It possesses hindlimbs that are very long relative to its forelimbs, similar to the related genus Hongshanornis. Longicrusavis has a more robust rostrum than the closely related genus Hongshanornis. The animal exhibits an obvious long, thin, and pointed beak.

Although no teeth are preserved, Longicrusavis likely had teeth in its upper jaw, indicated by alveoli in the premaxilla and maxilla. The absence of alveoli in the mandible suggests that Longicrusavis was likely edentulous in the lower jaw.
Comparison of tail feathers suggests Longicrusavis represents the oldest known bird form with a long, fan-shaped tail that improved flight.

The family name Hongshanornithidae honors the ancient Hongshan culture of China. The holotype specimen PKUP V1069 of Longicrusavis was found in the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation in Liaoning Province, China.
Longicrusavis was a ground-dwelling carnivore and wader that was a dominant species in the Jehol Biota ecosystem.
Longicrusavis is scientifically important because detailed evidence of the transition from dinosaurs to birds is rare.
The parent group of Longicrusavis is the family Hongshanornithidae. The type species of the genus Longicrusavis is Longicrusavis houi.

Longicrusavis provides evidence of small, specialized birds from the early Cretaceous, dating between 120 and 130 million years ago. Longicrusavis fossils originate from the earlier Yixian and Jiufotang Formation periods within the Jehol Biota. Longicrusavis lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
